The OIG has identified unlocked medication carts in several inspection reports.  Below are the reports that specifically mention this problem, with the citation and a link to the full report:

| Report (date) | Finding quoted from the report | Recommendation (summary) | Report link |
|---|---|---|---|

| **Combined Assessment Program Review – Atlanta VA Medical Center** (12 Mar 2014) – “We recommended that processes be strengthened to ensure that medication carts are secured at all times and that compliance be monitored.” | Same text as above. | Strengthen processes to keep carts locked and monitor compliance. | https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-atlanta-va-1 |
| **Combined Assessment Program Review – West Palm Beach VA Medical Center** (31 Mar 2015) – “On the CLC‑N unit, two medication carts were unlocked and unattended. See recommendation 8.” | “On the CLC‑N unit, two medication carts were unlocked and unattended.” | Recommendation 8 (see report) calls for securing the carts. | https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-west-palm-2 |
| **Care and Oversight Deficiencies Related to Multiple Homicides – Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center** (11 May 2021) – “In 2018, medication carts on ward 3A were not consistently secured as some were unlocked and unattended…” | Same quoted text. | Secure medication carts at all times; limit use of universal unlock codes. | https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/care-and-oversight-deficiencies-related-multiple-homicides |
| **Combined Assessment Program Review – Miami VA Healthcare System** (7 Dec 2012) – “We found several unsecured medications on top of a medication cart in an unlocked room…” | Same quoted text. | Secure medications and carts; remove unlocked storage rooms. | https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-miami-va-1 |
| **Combined Assessment Program Review – Charlie Norwood VA Medical Center** (28 Mar 2016) – “Three of seven patient care areas had unlocked medication cart drawers; expired medications; or undated, open multi‑dose vials.” | Same quoted text. | Recommend that employees secure medication carts when not in use. | https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-charlie-1 |

**Data as of 2026‑11‑04** (the latest dataset date returned by the OIG API).  

These reports show that unlocked medication carts have been a recurring finding across multiple VA facilities, and each includes a recommendation to lock the carts and monitor compliance.
